messages.subject: Error message in buildMCMC() step
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to estimate the parameters for an intrinsic Gaussian Car process based mixture model, but kept getting the same error in the buildMCMC() step, the error message says: 
Error in if (model$getVarNames(nodes = targetNode) == model$getVarNames(nodes = deparse(expr))) { : argument is of length zero

Here is my code and the output:

code <- nimbleCode({
  tau_mix[1] ~ dgamma(0.1,0.1);
  tau_mix[2] ~ dgamma(0.1,0.1);
  mu[1] ~ dnorm(0, sd=10^3);
  mu[2] <- mu[1]+theta;
  theta ~ T(dnorm(0,sd=10^3),0,)
  tau1 ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
  tau0 ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)
  s1[1:N] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau1, zero_mean = 1)
  s0[1:N] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:N], tau0, zero_mean = 1)
  for(i in 1:N) {
    p1[i]<-exp(s1[i])/(exp(s1[i])+exp(s0[i]))
    t[i]<-rbinom(1,1,p1[i])+1
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[t[i]],tau_mix[t[i]])
  }
})

L <- 730000
constants <- list(N = 170000, L = L, num = num_input, weights = rep(1, L),
                  adj = adj_input)
data <- list(y = res$data[[1]])
inits <- list(tau_mix=c(1,1),mu=c(0,3),theta=3, tau1 = 1, tau0=1,t=c(rep(1,170000)),s1=rep(1,170000),s0=rep(-1,170000))
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)
> Rmodel$getVarNames()
[1] "tau_mix" 
[2] "mu" 
[3] "theta" 
[4] "tau1"
[5] "tau0"
[6] "lifted_CAR_calcNumIslands_oPadj_oB1to730000_cB_comma_num_oB1to170000_cB_cP" 
[7] "s1"
[8] "s0" 
[9] "p1" 
[10] "t" 
[11] "lifted_d1_over_sqrt_oPtau_mix_oBt_oBi_cB_cB_cP_L13" 
[12] "y" 
[13] "adj" 
[14] "num" 
[15] "weights"

> configure_rmodel <- configureMCMC(Rmodel,print=T,monitors = c("tau_mix", "mu","theta", "tau1", "tau0", "t", "s0", "s1"))
===== Monitors =====
 thin = 1: tau_mix, mu, theta, tau1, tau0, t, s0, s1
 ===== Samplers ===== 
RW sampler (3) 
- theta 
- tau1 
- tau0 
conjugate sampler (3)
 - tau_mix[]  (2 elements) 
- mu[]  (1 element) 
CAR_normal sampler (2) 
- s1[1:170000] 
- s0[1:170000]

>build_model_MCMC <- buildMCMC(configure_rmodel)
Error in if (model$getVarNames(nodes = targetNode) == model$getVarNames(nodes = deparse(expr))) { : argument is of length zero

> compile_rmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel) 
compiling... this may take a minute. Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compilation details. compilation finished.

Where could be the problem in my code? There was no problem compiling the model. Any suggestions will be appreciated!

Ziqiao

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Error message in buildMCMC() step
parts:
John, thanks for your message.  The error was being triggered in some of the internal processing that takes place fo CAR nodes, but the root of the trouble is in your model specification.  In your model, you have the line:

 t[i] <- rbinom(1,1,p1[i])+1

I understanding it's tempting to use this construct in a model, to have t[i] be a valid binary indexing variable (taking values 1 or 2) used to index mu[].  However, as written, this won't function as you intend.  This becomes a deterministic node in NIMBLE (because of the <- assignment), which means the model functions simulate() and calculate() won't calculate densities for this node, as we'd want, and not to mention it threw off the internal processing that takes place with CAR nodes.

I tried replacing your code, you can choose a better variable name than I did, but replacing the line shown above with the two new lines:

tTEMP[i] ~ dbinom(size = 1, prob = p1[i])
t[i] <- tTEMP[i] + 1

Now, tTEMP is a stochastic node, and t[] is a derived deterministic node, which can be used as an index for mu[].  The other change you need to make is in the initial values list, to no longer provide an initial value for t[] (initial values for t[] will be deterministically calculated automatically), and instead add an initial value for tTEMP.  I used:

inits <- list(...., tTEMP = rep(0,N))

With this change, I think it all runs fine now.

Your issue raises an interesting point, about usage of random simulation functions (e.g., rbinom) inside model code, which we may not be clear about in the user manual.

Let me know if this works for you,
Daniel
